title: Stop, stabilize, signal

action.text: Pause on stable ground and check the scene before approaching an injured person. Check responsiveness, breathing and obvious life-threatening injury.
If someone is unresponsive, breathing abnormally or bleeding severely, call 911 and follow the dispatcher. Give your location and the immediate hazard.
If travel has stopped, use available shelter and insulation. Tell everyone where to wait and who is trying to make contact.

title: Stay, signal or move

action.text: Stop. If an immediate hazard threatens the spot, reach safer ground nearby only when you can identify a safe way there.
Contact 911 when help is needed and service is available. Report last known position, landmarks, number of people, injuries and any planned movement.
If you cannot determine a safe route, stay together in a findable location, shelter from weather and prepare to signal when responders are nearby.

Block convection with a windbreak or windproof shell, and limit evaporation by shedding damp cotton, venting sweat during work and keeping rain off insulation.

stop.text: Any suspected fuel, solvent, pesticide, heavy-metal or algal-toxin hazard requires immediate source abandonment and switching to an alternate safe supply.

diagram: Sheen, odor or runoff cue | Never taste to test | Abandon source and protect gear
visual: Failure-mode illustration separating visible/odor chemical cues from invisible dissolved toxins and showing mandatory gear/source rejection. Conceptual, not to scale.

title: Shift to alternative water supplies when local sources are unusable
origin: CDC advisories and emergency water supply; new manuscript

action.text: Inventory remaining sealed commercial water and verified potable household reserves (including safe drained water-heater tanks only if municipal supply was uncontaminated and power/fuel is shut off per official guidance).
Locate official municipal bulk-water distribution sites, neighboring uncontaminated utilities or alternate mapped watersheds reachable without creating travel hazards.
Reduce physical exertion and heat exposure while conserving safe drinking water; prioritize hydration for infants, older adults and medically vulnerable members.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Execute a structured fallback plan when chemical spills, algal blooms, drought or equipment failure eliminate local water sources.
applies: Household water disruptions, contaminated local lakes/wells and backcountry trips encountering dry or polluted sources.
equipment: Local emergency distribution info, vehicle/exit map, sealed potable reserve and communication device.

failure.text: Trying to push deeper into a dry or bloom-affected backcountry corridor or attempting risky improvised distillation of chemical-contaminated water.

verify.text: Confirm remaining safe liters, hours of margin and the exact safe route to an official potable refill or exit.

stop.text: Turn back or relocate early before safe drinking water runs out; never drink chemically contaminated water as a stopgap.

diagram: Audit remaining potable reserve | Cut heat and exertion loss | Relocate to verified supply
visual: Decision tree directing transitions from local source rejection to reserve auditing, exertion reduction and verified alternate potable sources. Conceptual, not to scale.

title: Escalate to emergency assistance when safe hydration cannot be maintained
origin: NPS emergency plan, ARC first aid and CDC water; new manuscript

action.text: Halt strenuous travel in shade or wind protection to slow fluid loss through sweat and respiration while assessing remaining safe water and exit distance.
Watch the group for worsening dizziness, confusion, inability to keep fluids down, minimal dark urination or heat illness—signs that require prompt medical help.
Contact 911, local emergency management or search and rescue early with your verified location, party size, water status and any medical or mobility needs.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Recognize severe dehydration or unresolvable water shortage early enough to summon help safely.
applies: Stranded outdoor parties or isolated households without safe water, working treatment or safe self-evacuation routes.
equipment: Phone, emergency communicator or NOAA radio, written location details and shade or thermal shelter.

failure.text: Waiting until severe confusion or heat stroke develops before calling for help, or drinking fuel- or bloom-tainted water out of panic.

verify.text: Confirm your location, water shortage duration and any medical symptoms have been communicated clearly to responders or emergency contacts.

stop.text: Confusion, collapse, severe heat illness or multi-day inability to obtain safe water is an emergency requiring immediate responder activation.

diagram: Halt exertion in shelter | Screen dehydration and heat signs | Call responders early with location
visual: Decision tree connecting unresolvable water shortage and symptom screening to early shelter stabilization and emergency rescue activation. Conceptual, not to scale.
reviewer: Wilderness medicine, public health and search and rescue

title: Confirm the starting point and first checkpoint
origin: B014 reconstruction · continuation of r01

action.text: Identify the trailhead on the map and match its name or another reliable feature to the location.
Identify the first decision point, such as a signed junction. Agree on what you expect to see before you proceed.
If the expected feature does not appear, stop and compare the last verified point with the actual surroundings. Avoid continuing just to find a matching landmark.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Establish one map-to-ground match before leaving the trailhead.
applies: A planned trip using a paper or offline map and a marked route.
equipment: Current map, trip plan and another reader to cross-check when available.

verify.text: Both the start and first checkpoint can be described in a way another party can use.

stop.text: If the start or route is uncertain, revise the plan before leaving known ground.

diagram: Match the trailhead | Predict first checkpoint | Compare on arrival
visual: Practice schematic with abstract checkpoints. Use actual park maps for field exercises.

title: Test offline maps and paper backup
origin: B014 reconstruction · continuation of r01

action.text: Obtain a current map that includes the planned route, nearby alternatives and identifiable roads or exits.
Disconnect the device from the network at home and open the full planned area. Confirm landmarks and scale remain readable.
Carry a paper map and use it to point to the same trailhead and route. Practice sharing a last confirmed position from paper.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Verify the route remains usable without coverage or power.
applies: Before a trip beyond dependable network service.
equipment: Downloaded map, map reader, paper map and independent power if used.

verify.text: The party can find the trailhead and two checkpoints using either map without network access.

stop.text: If the plan depends entirely on a device you cannot use offline, revise the route or kit before leaving.

diagram: Save relevant map area | Test without coverage | Match paper backup
visual: Independent map materials support the same route and landmarks.

title: Check carbon monoxide alarms before an outage
origin: Preparedness primer reconstruction · Home Resilience

action.text: Check whether there are CO alarms on each level and outside sleeping areas. Follow placement and maintenance instructions for each unit.
Check the test and backup-power procedure. Identify the agreed outdoor meeting point and make it known to everyone in the household.
If an alarm indicates carbon monoxide or exposure is suspected, get to fresh air immediately and contact emergency services.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Verify audible alarms and a family response before portable fuel equipment is needed.
applies: Household outage preparation and suspected carbon monoxide exposure.
equipment: CO alarms, exact manufacturer instructions and a household exit plan.

verify.text: The household knows the alarm sound, exit and where to call from outside.

stop.text: A working alarm does not make indoor generator or camp-stove use safe.

diagram: Verify alarms | Agree on exit | Fresh air and emergency help
visual: Prevention and evacuation checklist for a household rather than an alarm installation drawing.
reviewer: Carbon monoxide safety and emergency management

title: Match preservation plans to tested recipes
origin: Preparedness primer reconstruction · Small Acreage Self-Reliance

action.text: Find a tested recipe for the exact food and preparation. Distinguish low-acid foods that require a tested pressure-canning process from foods with other tested processes.
Match the jar size, ingredients and equipment to the recipe. Obtain its altitude adjustment before beginning.
If the recipe or equipment does not cover your ingredients, elevation or container, choose a different tested recipe or another approved preservation method.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Identify the exact tested process before preparing produce for shelf-stable storage.
applies: Household home canning. This card selects an authoritative recipe and gives no processing schedule.
equipment: Validated recipe for the food, container size and equipment. Determine local elevation.

verify.text: The recipe citation, equipment, jar size and altitude instructions agree before processing.

stop.text: Do not improvise processing time, pressure or ingredients to salvage an untested recipe.

diagram: Identify food and recipe | Confirm equipment and jar | Check altitude
visual: Canning process selection only; validated instructions control the actual process.

title: Track cold food during a power outage
origin: Preparedness primer reconstruction · Thirty-Day Outage Operations

action.text: Note when power went out and keep doors closed. A closed refrigerator typically preserves safe conditions for about four hours.
Check temperatures and elapsed time using the official chart. A closed full freezer generally holds temperature about 48 hours and a half-full one about 24 hours.
Evaluate each food by its category and storage history. For applicable frozen foods, ice crystals or a confirmed temperature of 40°F or below inform refreezing.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Use elapsed time and actual temperature to decide whether food can be kept.
applies: A household refrigerator or freezer initially working when the power fails.
equipment: Appliance thermometer, written outage log and access to the official per-item chart.

verify.text: Record the measured temperature and keep, refreeze or discard decision for each relevant food group.

stop.text: Never taste food to decide whether it is safe after a loss of cold storage.

diagram: Record power-off time | Keep doors closed | Apply official food chart
visual: Time and measured temperature together inform the per-item decision.
